paragraphs: Knowledge distillation trains a student language model using a teacher, but the reason different distillation methods work remains unclear. This paper studies them through interactions: nonlinear relationships among groups of input variables, such as words. Decomposing a model’s output score into these contributions provides a common language for comparing what students retain.

The authors identify interaction sparsification as a shared mechanism across the methods they examine. Students use fewer interactions when making predictions, while other interactions contribute zero effect. Differences in performance are associated with how methods handle complex interactions. A method typically performs better when it produces greater sparsity among these complex relationships, rather than simply preserving every contribution.

The paper turns this observation into Complex Interaction Penalty, an additional training loss that explicitly encourages complex interactions to become sparse. It can be added to different distillation methods. Experiments report consistent improvements on both in-domain and out-of-distribution benchmarks, supporting the usefulness of this interpretation as a guide for improving training.
icml-2026-a-unified-approach-to-interpre.tldr: Analyzing how distillation suppresses complex input interactions leads to an added loss that improves several distillation methods.

paragraphs: Static analysis reasons about program behavior without executing the program. Its precision depends partly on how it represents objects in memory. Traditional analyses use fixed rules for these representations, which can be restrictive for JavaScript’s varied object structures. ABSINT-AI introduces a language-model agent that helps choose an appropriate abstraction for each object.

The agent draws on cues such as object names and access patterns, allowing the analysis to adapt without encoding each cue as a handcrafted rule. Its authority is carefully bounded: it chooses within an interface and never directly changes program state. This design preserves the soundness guarantees of the underlying abstract interpretation while allowing more flexible representations.

The evaluation asks whether property accesses might encounter undefined or null values, a question relevant to compiler optimizations that remove unnecessary checks. ABSINT-AI reduces false positives by up to 34% against fixed-abstraction analyses. Ablations also report a 25% advantage over non-agentic model predictions, indicating that interaction with the analysis environment contributes materially to the results.
icml-2026-absint-ai-agentic-heap-abstrac.tldr: ABSINT-AI lets a bounded language-model agent adapt object representations, reducing static-analysis false alarms while preserving formal guarantees.

paragraphs: Constrained clustering uses information about pairs of examples to guide how data is grouped. Bayesian versions can struggle with large datasets and may offer little explanation of which features define each group. BASIL addresses these problems by learning cluster assignments and feature importance together, rather than treating feature relevance as a separate concern.

The framework uses stochastic variational inference to make this joint learning scalable. Its feature weights identify dimensions that distinguish clusters in ways consistent with the supplied constraints. Because those constraints can be noisy or contradictory, BASIL also adjusts their influence during training, reducing the weight given to unreliable supervision instead of treating every constraint equally.

Experiments on synthetic and real data report competitive clustering accuracy and more than 96% less training time on large datasets. The learned feature maps provide cluster-specific explanations. Robustness to as much as 30% noisy constraints is reported under sufficient supervision, an important condition on that finding. Applications include large-scale medical imaging and electronic health records.
icml-2026-basil-scalable-bayesian-semi-s.tldr: BASIL jointly learns clusters, relevant features, and constraint reliability to make Bayesian constrained clustering faster and more interpretable.

paragraphs: Decision-based image attacks estimate how to cross a model’s decision boundary using only its decisions. They often probe random directions to refine a small image perturbation. This paper identifies an inefficiency when sensitivity varies across input coordinates: with limited queries and one-bit feedback, noise can overwhelm improvements in coordinates that barely influence the prediction.

The authors model refinement as a stochastic dynamical system. Their analysis characterizes a stationary regime in which the perturbation aligns with the boundary normal in expectation, and its coordinate magnitudes reveal a local ranking of sensitivity. Reaching this regime does not generally produce the smallest possible Euclidean perturbation when the boundary is nonlinear.

Sensitivity-Aware Rescaling uses that remaining information. It derives an importance map from the best current perturbation and progressively suppresses low-importance regions, moving from coarse to fine adjustments. Experiments report consistent improvements in perturbation size, attack success, and visual imperceptibility. The contribution connects a theoretical account of stalled refinement to a practical way of reducing unnecessary image changes.
icml-2026-bias-in-zeroth-order-normal-es.tldr: Sensitivity-Aware Rescaling uses information left in noisy attack perturbations to suppress unimportant regions and improve decision-based attacks.

paragraphs: Forecasting several time series together requires combining variables that can change at different times and influence one another in changing ways. ConFlux tackles the mismatch between these heterogeneous inputs and the need for one coordinated forecast. It is designed as a general-purpose foundation model that adaptively integrates information across variables.

The model first rearranges variables to reduce entanglement between them. It then groups adjacent variables into compact patches, which a Vision Transformer-style architecture processes. This organization shortens the effective context and reduces attention complexity. The same token representation supports both pre-training and downstream forecasting, connecting the model’s general training setup to its later uses.

Across 25 public datasets, the authors report state-of-the-art performance in zero-shot forecasting, fine-tuning, and training from scratch. They also report faster inference and lower memory use. These findings suggest that organizing cross-variable information more compactly can benefit both forecast quality and computational efficiency across the evaluated settings, rather than requiring a separate representation for each training regime.
icml-2026-conflux-multivariate-time-seri.tldr: ConFlux rearranges and patches time-series variables to improve multivariate forecasting while reducing inference time and memory use.

paragraphs: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by proposing candidate tokens that a target model can accept. For image generation, low acceptance rates limit the benefit, while simply loosening acceptance rules can damage image quality. CSD addresses this tension by making acceptance depend on the content being generated, rather than applying the same relaxation everywhere.

Its acceptance mechanism uses entropy to account for differences in informational uncertainty across image regions. It raises acceptance rates in areas with little detail, where the method seeks opportunities to generate faster. An optimal resampling strategy accompanies this probability relaxation, making candidate handling part of the overall decoding design rather than an isolated change to the acceptance threshold.

CSD also includes a distribution alignment filter to keep generated outputs aligned with the target model’s distribution and improve quality. Experiments on Lumina-mGPT and Janus-Pro report advantages for the approach. The central idea is to coordinate regional acceptance flexibility with distribution alignment, addressing the quality problems that arise from relaxing speculative decoding criteria directly.
icml-2026-csd-content-aware-speculative-.tldr: CSD adapts speculative token acceptance to image content and adds distribution alignment to improve generation efficiency and quality.

paragraphs: Linear attention offers a less costly alternative to standard attention for long contexts. Some approaches retain several memory states to improve representation, but fixed rules for combining those states can obscure important tokens. Dynamic Linear Attention addresses this problem by adapting how memory is summarized as the information in a sequence changes.

Its first mechanism chooses state boundaries using token-level information variation. It preserves more detail near semantic transitions and compresses relatively stable stretches more aggressively. Its second mechanism keeps the state cache at a fixed size and in chronological order. When space must be managed, it selectively combines adjacent states with low information content.

Together, these mechanisms connect the allocation of memory detail to the sequence itself while bounding cache growth. The authors pre-train the framework on two different linear attention models and evaluate it on ten datasets across three aspects. They report improvements over state-of-the-art approaches, supporting adaptive state merging as a way to improve the evaluated models’ handling of long contexts.
icml-2026-dynamic-linear-attention-d0dae.tldr: Dynamic Linear Attention preserves detail around meaningful changes while selectively merging memory states to keep storage bounded.

paragraphs: Training web-search agents with reinforcement learning is expensive because their trajectories involve long contexts and costly interactions. Group-based optimization can also lose useful information when every rollout in a group receives the same reward. EVOLVING ROLLOUTS seeks to make previously collected trajectories useful beyond the training episode in which they were produced.

The framework distills reward-labeled trajectories into strategic experiences and supplies those experiences as contextual guidance for later behavior. Learning therefore occurs through both parameter updates and changes to the guidance available in the context. This allows zero-variance rollout groups to contribute information through the experience repository even when they provide no reward contrast for standard group-based optimization.

The authors report improved sample efficiency and task performance on web-search benchmarks. With this framework, Qwen3-8B exceeds Qwen3-30B-A3B in average performance across GAIA, xBench, and HLE, while Qwen3-4B obtains comparable results on GAIA and HLE. These findings support reusing historical experience as a practical complement to parameter-based reinforcement learning.
icml-2026-evolving-rollouts-harnessing-h.tldr: EVOLVING ROLLOUTS turns past web-search trajectories into contextual guidance, improving training efficiency and benchmark performance.

paragraphs: World models can learn hidden action representations from videos that have no action annotations. These latent actions provide controls for generating and manipulating videos. A common design uses one latent action for an entire scene, which becomes difficult when several entities act simultaneously and their changes must be represented together.

The Factored Latent Action Model, or FLAM, decomposes the scene into independent factors. Each factor infers its own latent action and predicts its own value at the next step. This distributes the dynamics modeling across factors, giving the model a more structured way to represent simultaneous changes than a single scene-wide action representation provides.

Experiments on simulated and real-world datasets with multiple entities report better prediction accuracy and representation quality than prior work. The authors also report improved video generation and benefits for downstream policy learning. These results support factorizing latent actions for the evaluated complex environments, connecting the structure of the learned dynamics to both predictive quality and their usefulness for later control tasks.
icml-2026-factored-latent-action-world-m.tldr: FLAM learns separate latent actions for scene factors, improving multi-entity video prediction, generation, and downstream policy learning.

paragraphs: Prototype-based federated learning shares class representations that help clients align their locally learned features. However, averaging local prototypes or refining global anchors can allow their meanings to drift across clients. FedHPro addresses this problem by learning global class representatives, called hyper-prototypes, that aim to preserve more consistent semantic information.

The key change concerns how these representatives are optimized. Gradient matching connects the hyper-prototypes to class-relevant characteristics distilled directly from clients’ real examples, rather than relying only on prototype-level summaries. FedHPro then uses mutual-contrastive learning with client-specific margins to separate different classes, alongside a consistency penalty that encourages representations within each class to agree.

Experiments cover several forms of data heterogeneity across clients. The authors report that hyper-prototypes provide a more semantically consistent global signal and that FedHPro achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets. The findings support improving the source of shared class information, as well as the objectives that use it, when aligning clients whose local data differ.
icml-2026-fedhpro-federated-hyper-protot.tldr: FedHPro uses gradient matching to learn shared class prototypes that provide more consistent guidance across heterogeneous federated clients.

paragraphs: Synthetic data can help federated clients compensate for differences in their local datasets. Existing augmentation methods often try to balance classes, implicitly assuming the global distribution is balanced too. FedPDG targets settings where that assumption fails and privacy constraints prevent the server from accurately measuring the true global distribution.

Its guiding observation is that a model’s performance carries information about the data on which it was trained. The method compares local and global model performance to identify regions where each client lacks data, then generates corresponding examples. It also adapts the diffusion generator using preference optimization so that generated data better matches the global distribution.

This makes augmentation responsive to discrepancies between models instead of treating equal class counts as the desired outcome. Experiments on multiple benchmarks report improvements over state-of-the-art methods, reaching up to 3.82%. The findings support using model behavior as an indirect signal for selecting and generating useful client data when the overall data distribution is unknown.
icml-2026-fedpdg-prediction-discrepancyg.tldr: FedPDG uses local–global model discrepancies to generate client data that better reflects an unknown, potentially imbalanced global distribution.

paragraphs: Animating a human image remains especially difficult around the hands, whose many possible movements make consistent generation challenging. Preference optimization offers a potential way to improve quality, but constructing reliable pairs of preferred and rejected hand animations is expensive. Frame-to-frame inconsistencies further complicate those comparisons, motivating a method that does not require paired preferences.

Implicit Preference Alignment is a post-training framework grounded in implicit reward maximization. It increases the likelihood of high-quality samples generated by the model itself while penalizing departures from the pretrained prior. This combines a signal favoring better outputs with a constraint that keeps adaptation connected to the model’s existing learned behavior.

A Hand-Aware Local Optimization mechanism directs the alignment process specifically toward hand regions. Experiments report improved hand generation through effective preference optimization while reducing the burden of constructing preference data. The contribution links a pair-free training objective with targeted local optimization, making the approach directly responsive to the animation region that motivated the work.
icml-2026-implicit-preference-alignment-.tldr: Implicit Preference Alignment improves animated hands using self-generated quality samples and local optimization without paired preference data.

paragraphs: Protein structure representations can mix many biological signals together, making it difficult to see which structural properties relate to function. ProtDiS reorganizes pretrained embeddings of protein micro-environments into dimensions guided by biological knowledge and the task at hand. Its goal is to make useful structural information more distinct and interpretable.

The framework draws on the information bottleneck principle, balancing how much relevant information a representation retains against how compact it becomes. This produces structural features described as more specific, independent, and information-efficient. Decomposition therefore serves both predictive modeling and interpretation: it changes how the representation organizes information rather than merely adding another downstream predictor.

Across twelve downstream tasks, the authors report consistent improvements, with the largest gains under structure-based splits. Analyses at protein and residue levels show distinctions between proteins with similar folds but different functions, along with fine-grained biophysical signals. These findings suggest that knowledge-guided decomposition can help organize protein latent spaces around meaningful structure–function relationships.
icml-2026-learning-protein-structure-fun.tldr: ProtDiS decomposes protein structure embeddings into biologically guided features, improving downstream predictions and interpretation.

paragraphs: Safe reinforcement learning must pursue useful long-term behavior while respecting safety constraints. A common approach combines reward and cost with a linear weighting, which offers limited guidance when their relationship is nonlinear. USB-RL instead learns an implicit preference over safety and performance from experience, avoiding manually tuned cost weights.

The method compares pairs of long-horizon outcomes without external supervision to infer a monotone partial-order score. This score provides a learned way to evaluate trade-offs rather than relying on one fixed linear formula. It then guides policy optimization inside a world-model framework, allowing multi-step planning over imagined outcomes with a dynamically learned balance.

Across diverse safety benchmarks, the authors report strong returns alongside substantially fewer safety violations, with stable and interpretable trade-offs. These results support learning how to compare safety and performance outcomes as part of model-based control. The empirical finding is improved behavior under the evaluated constraints; the abstract does not present the method as eliminating all safety violations.
icml-2026-learning-rewardcost-balance-in.tldr: USB-RL learns safety–performance preferences from long-term outcomes to guide world-model planning without manually tuned cost weights.

paragraphs: Language-model agents increasingly connect to applications through the Model Context Protocol, or MCP. Existing tool benchmarks largely emphasize generic information seeking, leaving a gap around tools tied to personal accounts and local databases. MCP-Persona introduces an evaluation focused on these personalized application settings, using environment simulation as described in the paper’s title.

The benchmark covers applications including Reddit, Xiaohongshu, Lark, and Slack. This range places personal social applications and workplace collaboration tools within the same evaluation effort. The defining distinction is that tool use occurs in an individual application context, so evaluating generic information access alone does not capture the practical challenge the benchmark targets.

Experiments with several state-of-the-art agents reveal substantial difficulty with personalized tool use. The benchmark’s contribution is therefore both an evaluation resource and evidence of a capability gap in the tested agents. Its public release makes this particular class of application interactions available for further assessment and improvement, extending evaluation beyond the generic tools emphasized by existing benchmarks.
icml-2026-mcp-persona-benchmarking-llm-a.tldr: MCP-Persona benchmarks agents on personalized application tools and finds substantial weaknesses in current agents’ performance.

paragraphs: An optimizer’s update rule can favor particular geometric patterns in parameter changes. Orthogonal Lion, or OLion, combines two such influences: spectral control from orthogonalized directions and coordinate-level control from sign updates. The aim is to approximate a large step that respects both types of constraints for matrix parameters.

OLion first constructs a Lion-style momentum direction, approximately orthogonalizes it with a few Newton–Schulz iterations, and then takes the sign of each entry. The resulting update approximates optimization over an intersection of spectral and infinity-norm constraint sets. The authors prove convergence under a diagonal-isotropy assumption that they describe as mild and verify empirically; the guarantee depends on that assumption.

Evaluations span language and vision training, including GPT-2 and Llama pretraining, SiT image pretraining, and supervised fine-tuning. Under comparable tuning, OLion matches or exceeds AdamW and Muon while retaining only momentum-level optimizer state. It also reduces optimizer mismatch when fine-tuning checkpoints pretrained with AdamW, connecting the proposed geometry to practical training and adaptation results.
icml-2026-olion-approaching-the-hadamard.tldr: OLion combines approximate orthogonalization and sign updates, delivering competitive training results with momentum-level optimizer state.

paragraphs: Choosing useful training text becomes increasingly important as high-quality public data becomes scarce. Static filters cannot respond to a model’s changing training needs, while some dynamic methods judge examples using raw gradients without accounting for the optimizer. OPUS evaluates candidate data according to the parameter updates the optimizer would actually produce.

It projects these effective updates onto a target direction derived from a stable, in-distribution proxy. This makes utility depend on both the current training state and the optimizer’s transformation of gradients. Ghost techniques and CountSketch support computational efficiency, while Boltzmann sampling maintains diversity in the selected data. The reported additional compute overhead is 4.7%.

The authors report improvements over previous selection methods across corpora, quality levels, optimizers, and model scales, covering both pretraining from scratch and mid-training. They also find potential for using the utility score as a static filter to remove toxic documents before training. That filtering result is presented as a possible additional use of the score.
icml-2026-opus-towards-efficient-and-pri.tldr: OPUS selects training data using optimizer-shaped update utility, improving selection across training settings with 4.7% additional compute.

paragraphs: Tool-using agents can carry implicit state across sessions, activate it through events, and pass it between agents. This paper formalizes these constructs as Persistent Semantic Entities, characterized by name binding, event triggering, and propagation across boundaries. Its evaluation spans 24 models from 11 families and examines susceptibility, persistence, detection, and propagation.

All models in the 20-model susceptibility panel are affected, at rates of 20–100%; removing name binding yields zero contamination in those tests. Persistence varies by contamination type. Preferences remain at 100% at t=10 in every model probed, and adopted instructions persist. Persona effects partly decay, while factual contamination self-corrects in some tested models and remains at ceiling in others.

Context-isolated self-verification reduces contamination by 20–79%, with a median reduction of 36.5%, without oracle references. Keyword detection produces systematic false positives, and contamination rises from 40% to 75% through a four-stage agent pipeline. The controlled results identify preference and instruction contamination as particularly persistent risks, while explicitly avoiding a general claim that factual contamination corrects itself.
icml-2026-persistent-semantic-entities-i.tldr: The study characterizes persistent, propagating contamination in tool-using agents and finds partial mitigation through context-isolated self-verification.

paragraphs: Low-rank tensor modeling seeks compact structure in multidimensional data. The widely used Tubal Nuclear Norm penalizes transformed singular values uniformly, without separately controlling which frequency components are active and how much complexity each active component contains. This can be restrictive when only a few frequencies carry substantial energy and those frequencies also have low-rank structure.

The paper introduces a tensor lp-Schatten-q quasi-norm with parameters p and q between zero and one, inclusive. It jointly regulates sparsity across frequencies and low-rankness within each frequency, giving explicit control over both levels. The formulation includes the Tubal Nuclear Norm as a special case and encompasses several existing regularizers.

The authors establish minimax error bounds under their dual spectral sparsity model and develop a reweighted algorithm for the resulting nonconvex optimization. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness and robustness on noisy tensor completion, Poisson tensor completion, and image clustering. The contribution joins a more flexible structural model with theoretical error analysis and an algorithm for using it.
icml-2026-refining-dual-spectral-sparsit.tldr: A new tensor regularizer separately controls sparsity across frequencies and low-rank structure within them, with theory and practical optimization.

paragraphs: Trajectory inference reconstructs hidden dynamics from snapshots taken at different times. In settings such as single-cell genomics, destructive measurements prevent following the same sample through time. Finitely many snapshot distributions therefore do not uniquely determine the distribution of complete trajectories, and predicting held-out snapshots gives only a limited view of inferred dynamics.

The paper develops a data-driven estimator of Kullback–Leibler divergence between probability measures over functions. Applied to trajectories, this compares distributions over entire paths rather than only their values at individual times. The framework is designed to remain computationally tractable at the scale of realistic snapshot datasets, making this broader comparison usable in practice.

On benchmarks with analytic KL values, the estimates closely match those values. Experiments with synthetic and real single-cell RNA sequencing data find that existing metrics often disagree, while path-space KL offers a coherent comparison and reveals differences especially where observations are sparse or absent. These results support a stronger evaluation criterion under partial observability, without resolving the underlying non-identifiability.
icml-2026-relative-entropy-estimation-in.tldr: A scalable estimator of path-space KL compares inferred dynamics beyond snapshots and reveals discrepancies hidden by existing evaluation metrics.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can improve vision-language reasoning, but its training cost limits adoption. This paper asks whether the changing alignment between text and visual attention can provide useful training signals. It examines where a model plans to attend, where it actually attends, and where it ideally should attend during reasoning.

From these patterns, the authors derive two lightweight measures. Predictive View Accuracy estimates how difficult a sample is, while Reasoning View Accuracy reflects the quality of the reasoning chain. FOCUS-RL uses these signals to automate the training curriculum and provide dense reasoning supervision, tying training decisions to the model’s multimodal behavior.

The framework is presented as a plug-in for vision-language model reinforcement learning. Across six benchmarks and multiple model families, it achieves 2.5–4 times faster convergence than vanilla GRPO and an average accuracy gain of 4.4. These results support using text–vision alignment to guide both which examples receive training attention and how reasoning is supervised.
icml-2026-seeing-is-solving-unlocking-ef.tldr: FOCUS-RL uses text–vision alignment signals to guide training, reporting faster convergence and better multimodal reasoning accuracy.

paragraphs: A model can predict the correct final code output while giving intermediate reasoning that does not match execution. StepCodeReasoner addresses this gap by supervising runtime states along the way. It automatically inserts structured print-based anchors into code, creating execution traces that turn intermediate predictions into verifiable training targets.

Its reinforcement learning algorithm, Dual-Granularity GRPO, assigns credit at two levels. It compares sampled execution trajectories with one another and shapes learning within each trajectory using downstream correctness. This connects overall execution success to the individual states leading toward it, making intermediate execution modeling an explicit part of the learning objective.

The reported 7B model reaches 91.1% on CRUXEval and 86.5% on LiveCodeBench, exceeding CodeReasoner-7B and GPT-4o in the stated comparisons. It also scores 82.9% on the execution-trace benchmark REval, above the listed 7B, 14B, and GPT-4o results. Code generation improves as well, with an average score of 64.8 versus 62.6 for CodeReasoner-7B across the reported generation benchmarks.
icml-2026-stepcodereasoner-aligning-code.tldr: StepCodeReasoner trains on verifiable intermediate execution states, improving reported code reasoning, trace prediction, and generation results.

paragraphs: Continual pretraining lets language models acquire new facts, but it can also erase knowledge learned earlier. This paper develops a theoretical account of how factual knowledge is acquired and retained over successive training. The analysis uses a single-layer Transformer with linear attention, providing a simplified setting for examining common continual pretraining methods.

Within that framework, regularization changes how quickly parameters converge without changing their underlying tendency to forget. Data replay changes the convergence dynamics themselves and stabilizes pretrained knowledge. This distinction explains why slowing parameter movement and reintroducing prior information can have different effects, with the theoretical claim grounded in the model studied.

The authors use this insight to design Selecting Tokens via attentiOn Contribution, or STOC. It identifies influential factual snippets and uses them to guide the generation of replay data. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets support the theoretical findings and show reduced catastrophic forgetting. The method connects an explanation of retention dynamics to a concrete strategy for choosing what to replay.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-continua.tldr: A simplified theory of factual forgetting motivates STOC, which selects influential factual snippets to guide generative replay.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks classify nodes using both node features and graph structure, but either source can carry misleading signals that fail under distribution shifts. TIDE examines this problem by separating information into three components: information specific to features, information specific to structure, and information shared jointly by the two.

The framework aims to retain the label-relevant portion of joint information while filtering spurious information specific to either source. The authors provide theoretical and empirical analyses favoring an information bottleneck objective over standard supervised learning for this detection task. Their analysis links it to higher confidence on familiar nodes and a larger entropy gap between familiar and out-of-distribution nodes.

Across seven datasets, TIDE reports up to a 34% improvement in FPR95 over strong baselines while maintaining competitive accuracy on in-distribution nodes. The results support explicitly controlling which feature–structure information is retained when learning to distinguish unfamiliar nodes. They connect the representation objective to both detection quality and preservation of ordinary node-classification performance.
icml-2026-what-information-matters-graph.tldr: TIDE separates feature, structure, and joint information to improve detection of out-of-distribution graph nodes.

paragraphs: Active mapping requires an embodied agent to choose where to explore while building an understanding of an unfamiliar environment. This paper uses a vision-language model to support mapping without task-specific training and to accept language-driven interaction. Its central representation combines omnidirectional semantic information with geometry aligned to a bird’s-eye view.

The agent selects informative candidate waypoints in two-dimensional image space, then back-projects them into executable three-dimensional metric actions. This lets the vision-language model make spatial choices through visual inputs while connecting those choices to movement. A depth-first exploration agent divides the scene into regions and organizes the selected waypoints into a topological tree.

Following that tree supports thorough exploration of large scenes. Without task-specific training, the method improves coverage by approximately 13.25% and AUC by approximately 14.00% over the strongest evaluated baseline, while enabling language-conditioned interaction. The findings support combining a fused visual representation, image-space waypoint selection, and structured exploration for the evaluated zero-shot mapping setting.
icml-2026-zero-shot-active-mapping-via-f.tldr: A vision-language mapping agent combines panoramic semantics, bird’s-eye geometry, and depth-first exploration to improve zero-shot scene coverage.
